title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync to review environment access, initial benchmark results, and next steps for pilot readiness. Main blockers: KMS integration for private logging, SSO service account perms, and a small model mismatch causing higher p95 latency. Agreed next steps include sending a minimal access checklist, running a short latency-only benchmark, and scheduling a performance deep dive next week.
next_steps: Redwood to send minimal access checklist and updated runbook by 2025-05-15
Customer to provide service account with VPC peering details by 2025-05-20
Run latency-focused benchmark (SE-led) and share results by 2025-05-19
Schedule performance deep dive with infra team week of 2025-05-26
action_items: Lena Park - Send access checklist and security docs - 2025-05-15
Marco Diaz - Run latency-only benchmark and share logs - 2025-05-19
Ethan Cole - Create service account & VPC peering details - 2025-05-20
Maya Singh - Confirm KMS requirements and provide contact for key mgmt - 2025-05-18
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: ok everyone thanks for joining, this is the weekly POC sync for GammaHealth, agenda is quick: access, results, blockers, next steps.
[00:08] Priya Raman: hi thanks, yes we got AE and SE from Redwood, i'm Priya, we've got limited time today so let's focus on the env readiness and that latency run you mentioned.
[00:18] Marco Diaz: hey all, Marco from Redwood infra, quick note — i ran the preliminary throughput test yesterday on the dedicated slice you gave us. saw p50 ~120ms, p95 ~620ms on the 8k context with the quantized model, which is a hair higher than expected.
[00:35] Ethan Cole: just to confirm, that was on our dev VPC with the peering right? we set up the tunnel yesterday but havent given the final service account perms yet.
[00:45] Marco Diaz: correct, it was using the temp creds you posted. i think two items are contributing: kv cache warming wasn't enabled for prefixes, and there's a fallback to fp16 kernels on a few layers which bumps latency.
[00:58] Maya Singh: can you clarify fp16 fallback — is that a security concern or perf only?
[01:03] Marco Diaz: perf only, it's kernel selection and quantization compatibility. we'll propose a kernel pin that avoids the fallback. Priya, do you have baseline SLA requirements?
[01:13] Priya Raman: we're aiming for p95 < 500ms for user-facing product flows; batch jobs can be higher. cost target is as discussed — under $0.008/token if possible after optimizations.
[01:24] Lena Park: noted. quick onboarding checklist status — Ethan, do you have the SSO/SAML SP metadata, and has the KMS team been looped in?
[01:32] Ethan Cole: SSO metadata yes, we haven't yet given Redwood the service account to create the peering. KMS is a bit pending — our security wants an architecture note before sharing keys to partners.
[01:43] Maya Singh: correct, we need to see how Redwood uses the key, logs, rotate policy. SOC2 stuff.
[01:49] Lena Park: understood, we'll send an architecture blurb and our KMS integration doc. Marco, any cfg changes for improving p95?
[01:55] Marco Diaz: yeah -- enable prefix/KV caching for common prompts, reduce max batch wait from 50ms to 20ms for low-latency routes, and pin the kernel selection for that specific model variant. Also suggest testing 4-bit quant profile in a canary; that drops token cost but may increase slight latency variance.
[02:12] Priya Raman: can we see separate numbers for streaming vs non-streaming? our UX team cares about first-byte latency.
[02:18] Marco Diaz: i can run a first-byte latency test. initial runs showed first-byte around 90ms, so that part is okay. the tail is where batching and kernel fallback matter.
[02:26] Lena Park: ok good. on data privacy — you asked about logs retention and audit. Maya?
[02:31] Maya Singh: we'd like logs to stay in our account and for any hosted telemetry to be opt-in. is private deployment an option for the POC?
[02:37] Lena Park: yes, Redwood Private is available, but it adds setup time. For the POC we recommended Dedicated with VPC peering to validate perf quickly; Private can be the next phase if compliance needs it.
[02:49] Ethan Cole: timeline wise, we prefer to finish basic perf validation this sprint and decide on Private vs Dedicated end of next sprint.
[02:56] Marco Diaz: that aligns. i'll prioritize the latency-only benchmark you asked for. small caveat: we need service account with role 'redwood-infer-runner' to avoid manual creds.
[03:06] Priya Raman: i'll push for that, but it may take a day or two with internal approvals.
[03:10] Lena Park: ok we'll keep moving on the items we can control. Marco — can you call out the specific test you'll run so Ethan can foretell permissions?
[03:18] Marco Diaz: sure — i'll run: a 1k request synthetic trace with 8k context, 50% streaming mode, measure first-byte, p50, p95, and token cost with current quant profile. will also run kernel-pinned run to compare. needs service account + peering.
[03:33] Ethan Cole: noted. about the service account, will it need kms:Decrypt permissions? our policy locks that down.
[03:40] Marco Diaz: we don't need direct decrypt for your keys; we request a wrapped key or node-level access. Lena, i'll send exact IAM lines.
[03:48] Lena Park: great. any anomalies in the logs you saw?
[03:51] Marco Diaz: two small transcription/metric issues: the token counter in our wrapper double-counted subword splits for emojis in the sample set, that inflated cost slightly. also one request timed out and retried which bumped p95.
[04:04] Priya Raman: can you reproduce the timeout? it's concerning.
[04:08] Marco Diaz: i think that was due to a burst of 10 concurrent long-context requests; once KV cache warmed, no more timeouts. we'll stress test to be sure.
[04:16] Maya Singh: for compliance, will you share a short note on how retries are handled and where retry logs live?
[04:22] Lena Park: yes, we'll include retry behavior in the runbook.
[04:25] Priya Raman: regarding cost — you mentioned 4-bit quant. any risk to output quality?
[04:30] Marco Diaz: small regression risk for some numeric or narrow-domain prompts; we recommend running a small eval set (we can help) before enabling for user traffic.
[04:38] Ethan Cole: do you have automated eval harness? cause we want to tie regressions to specific prompts.
[04:43] Marco Diaz: yes, Redwood Optimize has a lightweight eval runner we can run against your prompt bank — we'll propose a 200-prompt sanity set.
[04:50] Lena Park: ok next steps recap: Lena to send access checklist and KMS doc; Marco to run latency-only benchmark and kernel-pinned run; Ethan to provide service account + peering details; Maya to confirm KMS requirements.
[04:59] Priya Raman: sounds good, also please share the raw benchmark spreadsheet so our infra folks can review.
[05:05] Lena Park: we'll share the spreadsheet and a short writeup. Marco, anything else?
[05:09] Marco Diaz: just that i'll flag any regressed prompts if we try 4-bit. also i'll include p50/p95/timeouts per route.
[05:17] Maya Singh: and security doc please, include SOC2 artifacts where possible.
[05:21] Lena Park: we'll attach SOC2 summary and the integration checklist.
[05:24] Priya Raman: ok thanks everyone. are we scheduling the performance deep dive now or next week?
[05:29] Lena Park: let's sync on availability — I'll send a Doodle for the week of 2025-05-26.
[05:33] Ethan Cole: thanks, i'll try to get the service account before the 20th.
[05:36] Lena Park: awesome, thanks all. meeting adjourned.
notes: Shared artifacts to be sent: access checklist, KMS integration doc, SOC2 summary, benchmark spreadsheet. Next meeting: performance deep dive week of 2025-05-26.
